# Vendored sources

One directory per native backend, so each is self-contained and can be
refreshed independently:

| Directory | Backend | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `sail/` | `sail` | The pre-generated Sail model plus a patched Sail C runtime |
| `bochs/` | `bochs` | Upstream Bochs CPU sources at a pinned revision |

Both build with nothing but C and C++ compilers (C++20): no Sail toolchain, no
Bochs checkout, no autotools, no network. `build.rs` compiles whichever the
enabled cargo features ask for.

---

## `sail/` — the ACL2-derived formal model

- `model.cpp.gz` + `model.h` + `model_missing.cpp` — C++ generated by
  **Sail 0.20.1's `--cpp` backend** from
  [rems-project/sail-x86-from-acl2](https://github.com/rems-project/sail-x86-from-acl2)
  `model/` (master, 2026-07) plus this crate's `sail/harness.sail` (and with
  `logging.sail` replaced by `sail/quiet_logging.sail`), using the command in
  the README's "Regenerating the Sail model" section **followed by
  `scripts/fix_cpp_model.py`**. The model is a C++ class (`model::Model`): all
  architectural state is per-instance, which is what enables multiple
  independent oracles per process. License: BSD-3-Clause (Sail translation,
  Patrick Taylor / Thomas Bauereiss) AND BSD-3-Clause (original ACL2 X86isa
  model, Regents of the University of Texas; see the upstream `model/LICENSE`).

- `sail/runtime/` — the Sail C runtime (`sail.c`, `rts.c`, `sail_failure.c`,
  `sail_config.c`, `cJSON.c` + headers) copied from the `sail` 0.20.1 opam
  package, **with patches** (all marked `PORTABILITY PATCH` /
  `REENTRANCY PATCH` / `CPP-BACKEND PATCH`) — identical to, and taken verbatim
  from, sail-aarch64-oracle's vendored runtime:
  - arbitrary precision goes through the bundled **mini-gmp/mini-mpq** instead
    of system GMP (define `SAIL_SYSTEM_GMP` to switch back);
  - `gmp_*printf`/`gmp_sscanf`/`asprintf` replaced with portable equivalents;
  - POSIX `clock_gettime` → C11 `timespec_get`; `getline` fallback for
    Windows; `getopt` stubbed under MSVC;
  - `elf.c` dropped entirely (nothing in the model references it), which also
    removes the zlib dependency;
  - `setup_rts`/`cleanup_rts` refcounted (multiple model instances share the
    process-wide runtime);
  - inline aliases `sint`/`sub_vec_int` for primitives the cpp backend calls
    under different names than the C backend;
  - **LLP64 fix** (`sail.h`): on Windows `unsigned long` is 32-bit, so the
    eight affected GMP entry points are macro-redirected to 64-bit-safe inline
    versions there.

  License: BSD-2-Clause (Sail authors); cJSON is MIT.

- `sail/runtime/mini-gmp.{c,h}`, `mini-mpq.{c,h}` — from **GMP 6.3.0**.
  ⚠️ License: **dual LGPLv3+ / GPLv2+** — unlike the rest of this backend (BSD).
  Statically linking it is fine for internal use; for distribution, LGPL §4
  obligations apply, or build with `SAIL_SYSTEM_GMP` + system libgmp (same
  license situation) — GMP simply is LGPL either way.

`model.cpp.gz` (~9 MB → ~1 MB) is decompressed into `OUT_DIR` at build time.
`SAIL_MODEL_C` / `SAIL_LIB_DIR` override the model and runtime for anyone
building against a freshly generated one.

To regenerate after editing `sail/harness.sail`, follow the README section
(which ends with `fix_cpp_model.py`), then refresh with:

```sh
gzip -9 -c /path/to/sail-x86-from-acl2/model/cpp/model.cpp > vendor/sail/model.cpp.gz
cp /path/to/sail-x86-from-acl2/model/cpp/model.h \
   /path/to/sail-x86-from-acl2/model/cpp/model_missing.cpp vendor/sail/
```

The runtime is independent of the generated model — only re-copy
`sail/runtime/` if you upgrade Sail itself, and then re-apply the patch hunks.

---

## `bochs/` — the Bochs CPU core

Upstream Bochs sources at a pinned revision, **unpatched**, compiled directly by
`build.rs`: `cpu/` and its subdirectories (decoder, fpu, avx, cpudb,
softfloat3e) plus four emulator support files (`logio.cc`, `pc_system.cc`,
`gui/siminterface.cc`, `gui/paramtree.cc`) that the CPU core calls into.

`bochs/PROVENANCE` records the exact upstream commit, the retrieval date and
the `./configure` flags behind the generated `config.h` / `bxversion.h`, with a
note on why each flag matters. Refresh with `sh scripts/vendor-bochs.sh`;
`BOCHS_DIR` overrides the source root.

That `config.h` was generated on Linux, so it also records *that host's* answers —
`MSVC_TARGET 0`, `strcasecmp` and `<dlfcn.h>` present, 64-bit `long`. For an MSVC
target `build.rs` rewrites those few lines into a copy it force-includes
(`msvc_config_header`), leaving the vendored file untouched; the rest of Bochs
(`osdep.h` in particular) already knows what to do once `config.h` describes the
platform honestly.

License: **LGPL-2.1-or-later** (`bochs/COPYING`). Because the result is
statically linked, shipping this source tree alongside a binary is what
satisfies the LGPL — keep `vendor/bochs/` with any redistribution.
